This turn I added Fig 6 (the λ clip), a decomposition table, and the strongest-valid-baseline columns in Table 1. The pushes are `e82eee5` on `figtab-repo` main and `7382678` on `paper-repo` dev. I checked that the changed Table 1 fits 6.75 in with no overfull box. A full `paper-repo` build still stops on a missing file (see below), so I did not get a clean full-document build.

- **Fig 6 (`fig_clip`):** it is drawn from `clip_sweep.csv` and `clip_real.csv`, which experiment-repo had already pushed in its own schema, so I used them as they are.
  - **Left panel:** the paired width ratio of unclipped to package PPI++ against the slope b. The synthetic sweep is plotted with the exact formula as a line, and the real sets are marked at their reference n.
  - **Right panel:** coverage of both intervals.
  - **Formula versus measured:** the line is the formula for the population-optimal tuning, while the markers include the estimation of λ. They part at small n (for example n = 30, b = 1, where the unclipped interval is wider), and the figure shows that. Only the σ = 0.6, N = 10 000 cells are drawn; the rest are counted in the caption note.
- **`tab_decomp` (appendix):** from `decomp.csv`, one row per arm on the same draws. It splits the width ratio into the SD ratio of the point estimates and the standard-error calibration (SE/SD), with coverage. The two `recentred` arms equal the package PPI++ to 1e-9 in every cell, so the table leaves them out and says so.
- **Table 1 (`tab_main`):** the second block now gives the headline arm's ratio and class against the strongest valid baseline of Outline rev. 9. A `base` column shows which baseline was used, and a double dagger marks cells where neither baseline passes the coverage rule. The calibrated-spline ratio column moved to `tab_headline_full` so the block still fits.
- **Other figures:** I did not re-commit them, because their caption notes (the numbers drawn) did not change. The PDFs are not byte-identical between runs, since the TeX route gives random font-subset tags.
